title: A new class of colored Gaussian graphical models with explicit normalizing constants: the characterisation of RDAG-admitting colored graphs (Theorem 6.1)
author: Adam Chojecki, Piotr Graczyk, Hideyuki Ishi, Bartosz Ko{\l}odziejek
work: A new class of colored Gaussian graphical models with explicit normalizing constants
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 6.1 (source0.tex lines 2264--2270, source label thm:RDAG), the iff-characterisation 'Let (G,C) be a colored graph. Then (G,C) admits an acyclic orientation whose inherited coloring is compatible and for which (i)--(iii) in (6.1) hold if and only if (G,C) is a symmetric CER graph and G has no edges between vertices of the same color', delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 3490--3536 (47 lines, one proof environment carrying the optional argument 'Proof of Theorem 6.1', detached only because the article prints it in the appendix). The theorem is a genuine structural characterisation: it identifies the combinatorial class of colored graphs admitting a compatible acyclic orientation satisfying three isomorphism conditions with the symmetric CER graphs without monochromatic edges. Both directions of the proof are substantive. In the forward direction the author selects an inverse topological order whose color classes are consecutive blocks, converts the absence of induced i->k<-j with i,j non-adjacent into a perfect elimination ordering of the skeleton, shows monochromatic edges are impossible, and then proves that conditions (ii)-(iii) are equivalent to 2-path regularity by a common-child counting argument for m_{v<->w} that must also handle loops and symmetrisation of unordered incoming color pairs. In the converse direction the author orients every edge from the later to the earlier color class, verifies acyclicity and the inverse topological property, derives the perfect elimination ordering from the cpeo condition, recovers compatibility from the lemma on equally colored edges, and again converts 2-path regularity into (ii)-(iii) through the same counting interpretation. That mixture of elimination-order theory, DAG orientation and 2-path counting is not a qualifying-exam exercise. H2: a complete original research-paper structural theorem with a two-direction proof of moderate length, whose core steps are genuine combinatorial constructions rather than routine verifications.
